audit.whatIsWrong: The chart and the prose contradict each other and the data. content.win is ['Trundle' x7] and every phases[].side is 'Trundle', while whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], early and mid all state Garen wins levels 2 through 5 ('he wins the short trade every time in this window'). The packet has Trundle at 48.48% over 559 games — the largest sample in the slice and a losing matchup.
audit.why: Garen's Decisive Strike is an 8s cooldown that breaks every slow on him and silences the next cast; against a champion whose only sticking tools are two slows, that genuinely owns levels 2-5. A chart giving Trundle all seven stages cannot be squared with a sub-50% win rate.
audit.corrected: No side or rating was changed — see notes and the question raised for the user, because those fields are short tokens and any rewrite of 'Trundle' to 'Garen' falls outside the applier's length band. The prose was left saying what it already correctly says (Garen owns 2-5) and sharpened with the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike warns about Garen's regen and Sterak's-style items but never mentions Demacian Justice, which is the actual thing that kills a Trundle who trades his health bar down.
audit.why: Riot's Demacian Justice text: 'Garen calls upon the might of Demacia to attempt to execute an enemy champion' — true damage, 120/100/80, 400 range. The interaction file flags Garen under both 'bypasses stacking resistances' and 'threatens a threshold kill'. Trundle's whole level-6 plan is stealing armour, and none of it applies to R.
audit.corrected: Demacian Justice named in the late spike and in mid, with the point that only your health bar moves the threshold.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup-defining interaction is absent. Decisive Strike does not only silence — Riot's text is 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him'. Trundle's only tools for holding Garen in Frozen Domain are the Chomp slow and the Pillar slow, and one 8-second button removes both and hands him the move speed to leave the zone. The page mentions the silence six times and the slow-break zero times. Also: wants.you[0] says 'Chomp's AS debuff' — Chomp saps Attack Damage. And whys[3] gives Courage a '~23 second' cooldown; it is 22 at rank 1.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon. Decisive Strike: 8s flat, 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him. His next attack... deals bonus damage and silencing them.' Courage: 22/19.5/17/14.5/12, 'a shield and tenacity for a brief moment followed by a lesser amount of damage reduction'. Chomp: 'briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage'. Perseverance regenerates only when he has not recently been struck — Chomp's 3.5s cooldown is short enough to hold it off permanently, which is worth stating as the positive counter.
audit.corrected: The slow-break written into the cooldown block, the report, the level-2-3 spike, the wants and early. AD sap corrected. Courage's real 22s stated. Perseverance denial framed around Chomp's 3.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage is the tracked cooldown but the only number on the page is a wrong one ('~23 seconds'), and Decisive Strike — the 8s button that actually breaks the lane open — has none.
audit.why: Decisive Strike 8s, Courage 22s at rank 1, Judgment 9s, Demacian Justice 120s.
audit.corrected: 8s / 22s / 120s now stated in the cooldown block, the dos, the report, the spikes, mid and whys[3].

edits.before: At level 1 you have a genuine poke tool in Chomp, but Garen's lane is built to absorb one trade and walk away healthier than it looks — his passive regen kicks in the moment he steps back, and you have no way to cancel it from range. Land your Q on every cannon minion last-hit attempt and deny him free steps-up, but do not commit to a level-1 all-in because Decisive Strike's silence arrives before you can establish Frozen Domain. Level 2 is where the matchup turns against you early: Garen gets Decisive Strike plus Courage on the same recall timing, which means the next time you drop W and step forward, he silences your Q mid-rotation and then pops W to shrug the attack speed punish. Your only answer is to place Frozen Domain first, force him to walk into it to last-hit, and bite him when he arrives — do not chase him out of the zone once he starts moving away or you eat a clean Judgment spin with no Q to answer it.
edits.after: At level 1 you have a genuine poke tool in Chomp, but Garen's lane is built to absorb one trade and walk away healthier than it looks — Perseverance restarts the moment he steps back. Land Q on every last-hit attempt and deny him free step-ups, but do not commit to a level-1 all-in because Decisive Strike's silence arrives before you can establish Frozen Domain. Level 2 is where the matchup turns against you: Garen gets Decisive Strike plus Courage on the same timing, so the next time you drop W and step forward he silences your Q mid-rotation and pops the shrug. The silence is only half of it — that same 8-second Q breaks every slow on him, so the Chomp slow you were counting on to hold him in the ice simply falls off and he leaves with bonus move speed. Place Frozen Domain first, make him walk into it to last-hit, and bite him when he arrives — never chase him out of the zone.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the grind: Garen is running short-trade patterns that his passive regen rewards and you are running extended-trade patterns that require him to stay in Frozen Domain longer than he wants. The key read is Courage's animation — if you see the golden flash, give the trade immediately and let him walk away, because fighting into a Courage W with your AS-steal still ramping is a net loss. At level 6 the lane inverts: Subjugate into Garen is genuinely strong because even a bruiser-itemizing Garen has enough armor and MR for the resist-drain to flip the duel. R early in the all-in — you want every Chomp that follows to benefit from the stolen resistances. Use Pillar of Ice to cut off his disengage after the first Subjugate hit so he cannot reach tower and coast on passive regen until you are on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the grind: Garen runs the short-trade patterns his Perseverance regen rewards and you run extended-trade patterns that need him to stay in Frozen Domain longer than he wants. The key read is Courage's animation — if you see the golden flash, give the trade and let him walk, because fighting into a 22-second Courage with your AD sap still ramping is a net loss. At level 6 the lane inverts: Subjugate into Garen is genuinely strong because even a bruiser-itemising Garen has enough armor and MR for the resist-drain to flip the duel. R early so every Chomp after it benefits. Watch his R too — Demacian Justice is true damage, so stolen armour does nothing against it and only your health bar moves the threshold. Pillar of Ice cuts his disengage after the first Subjugate hit so he cannot reach tower and coast on regen.

edits.before: Courage is off cooldown every ~23 seconds and Garen uses it to cut off your entire Frozen Domain window — trade only when you see it down or baited, or concede the health bar.
edits.after: Courage is back every 22 seconds at rank 1 and Garen uses it to cut off your entire Frozen Domain window — trade only when you see it down or baited, or concede the health bar.

notes: The decisive interaction was missing entirely: Decisive Strike 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him' on an 8-second cooldown. Trundle's only tools for holding Garen inside Frozen Domain are the Chomp slow and the Pillar slow, and one button removes both — the page named the silence six times and the slow-break zero times. It is now in the cooldown block, the report, the level 2-3 spike, two wants and the early block, with the correct caveat that the pillar's TERRAIN survives even though its slow does not. Also added Demacian Justice (true damage, 120s) which appeared nowhere despite the interaction file flagging Garen for both resistances-invalidated and execute-threshold. Fixed 'Chomp's AS debuff' (it saps AD) and Courage's cooldown ('~23 seconds' — it is 22 at rank 1). NOT changed, and raised as a question instead: content.win is ['Trundle'] seven times and every phases[].side is 'Trundle', while this entry's own whys[1]-whys[3], early and mid all say Garen wins levels 2 through 5, and the packet has Trundle at 48.48% over 559 games. The chart is the part that looks wrong, but 'Trundle' to 'Garen' is a 7-character to 5-character change and the applier's +/-10% length band would reject it, so it needs a decision rather than a proposal.
